The function `render_blog_post` takes the components of a blog post (author, title, content and tags) and returns an HTML string that is safe from XSS attacks. All user‑supplied text is escaped with `html.escape`, and each tag is wrapped in a `` element. """ import html # Example format string. Parameters ---------- author_id : str Identifier of the post's creator. post_heading : str Heading/title of the post. content : str Main body text of the post. labels : list[str] List of tags/labels associated with the post. Returns ------- str The rendered HTML string, fully escaped to prevent XSS. Raises ------ TypeError If any of the arguments are not of the expected type. """ # Basic type validation if not isinstance(author_id, str): raise TypeError("author_id must be a string") if not isinstance(post_heading, str): raise TypeError("post_heading must be a string") if not isinstance(content, str): raise TypeError("content must be a string") if not isinstance(labels, list) or any(not isinstance(l, str) for l in labels): raise TypeError("labels must be a list of strings") # Escape all user‑supplied data esc_author = html.escape(author_id, quote=True) esc_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=True) esc_content = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Render tags: each tag is wrapped in a , escaped individually rendered_tags = ''.join( f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in labels ) # Fill the template rendered_html = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( author_id=esc_author, post_heading=esc_heading, content=esc_content, labels=rendered_tags ) return rendered_html # Example usage (remove or comment out in production) if __name__ == "__main__": html_output = render_blog_post( author_id="user123", post_heading="", content="This is a bold move!", labels=["python", "security & privacy"] ) print(html_output)
